static_traits.name: Lin Yazhi
static_traits.occupation: Hollywood male model volunteer (aspiring to become a male model)
static_traits.social_status: Has interpersonal support (friends to talk to), but has not yet discussed specific worries with friends; interpersonal relationships affected by fear of being judged as 'the sick kid'
static_traits.medical_history: Had urinary system cancer at 18 and completed treatment; currently no significant physical illness; has not yet received psychotherapy
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, capable of self-reflection and describing concrete situations; fairly cooperative but skeptical; emotional experience dominated by anxiety; cautious on social topics, prone to worry

basic_info.main_problem: I worry people will always see me as the 'sick kid' who had cancer, which leaves me long-term anxious and worried, especially in social situations.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because these feelings of being labeled the 'sick kid' are starting to affect my confidence and ambition to become a male model.
growth_experiences: Experienced and beat urinary system cancer at 18. After treatment ended I did not yet feel relieved, as stress from health uncertainty was high, and anxiety and worry have persisted since. Especially prominent in social situations (meeting new friends, attending events), gradually developing into fear of others' judgment and excessive self-consciousness, affecting interpersonal relationships, career confidence, and eating and sleep.

core_beliefs: I will always be seen as the sick child
My worth will be overshadowed by my medical history

special_situations.event: When meeting new friends at social occasions or attending activities
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others know I once had cancer, they will look down on me and see me only as 'the sick kid' rather than the whole me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Self-soothing and distraction (keeping busy through work), reducing self-exposure and avoiding in-depth communication
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They must be looking down on me inwardly, seeing me only as that kid who was sick

special_situations.event: At industry social or networking events (such as last week's networking event)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I am treated as 'the sick kid', others won't judge me by looks or ability, and I will never get opportunities in the modeling industry
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Leaves early, lowers participation to avoid being scrutinized
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will be judged by my medical history rather than my ability, and it will only get worse

special_situations.event: When no one directly mentions my medical history at social events
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I feel intense tension and discomfort, it means they are judging or gossiping about me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Continuing self-monitoring and inner rumination, struggling to stay present
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I feel terrible; this must mean they are talking about me behind my back

special_situations.event: When thinking about talking to friends about one's specific worries
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I express worries, I will burden others and be viewed negatively
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids talking about it, keeps worries pressed in his heart, bears them alone
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I shouldn't trouble others; they'll think something is wrong with me

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be seen as a 'complete and capable person', to be accepted and recognized interpersonally and professionally (evaluated by talent, appearance and effort)
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being belittled, rejected, and losing opportunities after being labeled 'the sick kid'
defense_goal: Reduces the chance of being judged by avoiding in-depth socializing
Keeps worries pressed in the heart to maintain outward stability and safety
Distracting anxiety and self-focus by staying busy

object_relations.self_representation: A fragile self easily labeled (may be defined by others through medical history at any time)
object_relations.object_representation: Others as potential judges and rejecters (who look down on and negate me)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When discussing or entering social settings, especially networking and industry events
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Others will see me with the label 'sick child' as in the past and are secretly judging me (transference: bringing the expectation of being judged into the current relationship)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Maintain an empathic and steady tone, inviting examination of evidence and possibilities; use open-ended questioning, guiding differentiation of feelings from facts, gently challenging 'mind reading' assumptions.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When thinking about expressing specific worries to friends or others
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing that speaking up will burden others and invite negative judgment
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Gently explore as-yet-unexpressed worries in a supportive tone, providing a safe frame; encourage small steps of sharing, affirming their pace and boundaries.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When asked why I don't discuss this with friends or when making excuses to leave early
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: I shouldn't trouble others; they may not want to listen (self-justification for avoidance and withdrawal)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Gently label the rationalization tendency, inviting differentiation of 'caring for others' from 'self-avoidance'; use concretizing and reattribution techniques to explore more possible understandings.

manifestations: Hard to open up to others and build intimate relationships
Stays guarded at social activities and leaves early
Having friends yet not discussing specific worries, choosing to bear it alone
outcomes: Sleep and eating disrupted, overall decreased quality of life

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact.
manifestations: Highly self-conscious and tense in social settings
Carefully avoids in-depth exchange to reduce the risk of being scrutinized

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves.
manifestations: Choosing to bear it alone rather than expressing specific worries to friends
Suppressing the need for expression on the grounds of 'I shouldn't trouble others'

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others.
manifestations: Assuming others look down on or gossip about me without evidence
Attributing inner shame and anxiety to others' negative views

positive_force: Has social support resources (friends to talk with)
Willing to try identifying and challenging negative thoughts, accepting reframing exercises
Can notice and name cognitive patterns (mind reading, overgeneralization, mental filtering)
Has overcome a major illness, showing resilience and persistence
negative_force: Worries about caring excessively about others' evaluations and being labeled
Cognitive distortions like mind reading, predicting the future, and emotional reasoning reinforcing anxiety
Avoidance and self-hiding in social settings (leaving early, reducing communication)
Sleep and eating rhythms disturbed, further lowering mood and functional state

target_behavior.behavior: High anxiety and leaving early at social events
antecedent: Meeting new friends or attending social/industry events
Thinking others may know or talk about one's past illness history
target_behavior.core_reason: Worrying about being labeled 'the sick kid' and belittled, rejected, hence catastrophic and mind-reading tendencies
target_behavior.function: Escaping judgment and negative emotional experiences, quickly lowering present anxiety
target_behavior.consequence: Missing connections and opportunities, hindered career development, interpersonal relationships staying shallow

target_behavior.behavior: Not expressing specific worries to friends, choosing to bear it alone
antecedent: Thinking about discussing my anxiety or medical-history-related worries
Facing opportunities for intimate interaction or seeking support
target_behavior.core_reason: Worrying about burdening others and being viewed negatively, tending to rationalize and repress emotional needs
target_behavior.function: Avoids possible embarrassment or being judged, maintaining surface stability and a sense of control
target_behavior.consequence: Social support not yet fully utilized; sense of isolation and anxiety persist or even worsen
